standard.title: Layout and navigation features
standard.description: identify the purpose of layout features in print and digital texts and the words used for headings and hyperlinks
standard.prior_knowledge: Students navigate print and screen texts using structural and navigation features (AC9E2LA05). They have not yet focused on identifying the purpose of specific layout features and the language choices made for headings and hyperlinks.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the purpose of layout features in print and digital texts including headings, subheadings, chapter headings and hyperlinks.

nodes.label: Purpose of headings and subheadings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify headings and subheadings in print and digital texts and explain what purpose each serves for the reader.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two headings or subheadings in an informative text and explain what purpose each serves for the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the words used as headings and subheadings in digital and print information texts and chapter headings in narratives, explaining how each guides the reader.
wider: Compare the words chosen as headings across two information texts on the same topic and discuss how different heading choices change what the reader expects
Create alternative headings for sections of a text and evaluate which heading best serves the reader's needs
success_criteria: Student names the type of layout feature (heading, subheading, chapter heading)
Student explains what the feature does for the reader — not just that it 'tells you what's there'

nodes.label: Hyperlinks in digital texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify hyperlinks in digital texts and explain the language choices made for hyperlink words and their purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one hyperlink in a digital text and explain what the hyperlink word signals to the reader about where it will lead.
nodes.typical_width: Examine the words used as hyperlinks in digital texts and explain how the language choices signal what the reader will find if they follow the link.
wider: Compare how hyperlink words in a children's website versus a news website differ in their language choices, and discuss what this reveals about audience
Discuss how hyperlinks change the way a reader moves through a digital text compared with a print text — and what this means for navigation
success_criteria: Student identifies a hyperlink and explains what the hyperlink word tells the reader
Student explains how the hyperlink serves a navigational purpose for the reader
